facts.statement: The genus Toxoprion was described by Hay in 1909.
Fossils of Toxoprion date from the Early Carboniferous to the Late Permian.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Carboniferous to Late Permian

facts.statement: Toxoprion fossils are found in marine strata near Eureka, Nevada.
facts.quote: whose fossils are found in marine strata from the Early Carboniferous until the Late Permian near Eureka, Nevada

facts.statement: Toxoprion is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalans.
facts.quote: Toxoprion (Ancient Greek for "bow saw") is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalans

facts.statement: Toxoprion had heavily serrated teeth growing outwards on the lower jaw symphysis like a rounded saw.
facts.quote: had its heavily serrated teeth grow outwards on the symphysis of the lower jaw similar to a rounded saw

facts.statement: Unlike Helicoprion, the tooth row of Toxoprion forms a downward curved whorl rather than coiling back on itself.
facts.quote: the tooth row of Toxoprion does not coil back on itself, as seen in Helicoprion, but instead forms a downward curved tooth whorl

facts.statement: Smaller teeth at the front of the whorl were juvenile teeth, while larger teeth at the back were grown in adulthood.
facts.quote: the smaller teeth found near the anterior end of the whorl represent the oldest teeth, which the animal grew as a juvenile and the larger and younger teeth found near the back of the whorl represent teeth grown in adulthood

facts.statement: Rounded older teeth and sharper younger teeth may indicate feeding damage or a dietary change with age.
facts.quote: its older anterior teeth typically appear more rounded than the younger and sharper teeth near the back of its whorl. This may represent damage from feeding or may signify a change in diet and/or feeding strategy with age

facts.statement: The name Toxoprion comes from Greek words meaning "bow" and "saw," referring to its bow-shaped jaw and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: The genus acquired its name from the Greek word τόξο (tóxo), from the bow-shaped jaw on which the teeth of the creature were arranged, and πριόνι (prióni), for the number of triangular serrated teeth it had

facts.statement: Toxoprion belongs to the parent group Helicoprionidae.
Toxoprion is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Toxoprion lived between 298.9 and 274.4 million years ago, from the Asselian to the Kungurian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Asselian to Kungurian (298.9 to 274.4 million years ago)
